subject: Biology
title: The Lymphatic System
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Lymphatic System usable.

hook.text: Your lymph nodes swell when you're sick—because they're filtering pathogens and activating immune cells.

buildup.text: The lymphatic system is a network of vessels, nodes, and organs that circulates immune cells.

discovery.text: Lymph nodes are checkpoints where antigens are presented to T and B cells, triggering responses.

twist.text: The spleen filters blood the same way lymph nodes filter lymph—removing old cells and pathogens.

climax.text: Without the lymphatic system, immune cells couldn't patrol, communicate, or reach infection sites.

punchline.text: Swollen lymph nodes mean your body is fighting. And winning.

quiz.question: Why do lymph nodes swell during an infection?
options: They're filtering pathogens and activating immune cells

details.summary: The lymphatic system is a network of vessels, nodes, and organs that drains excess fluid from tissues, filters pathogens through lymph nodes, and transports immune cells throughout the body. Lymph nodes swell during infections because they are actively filtering and fighting pathogens.
details.whyItMatters: The lymphatic system is the highway that connects immune organs and enables immune cells to survey the entire body. Lymph node examination is a standard diagnostic tool, and lymphatic dysfunction causes immune deficiency and severe fluid accumulat...
takeaways: Lymph nodes filter pathogens and are sites where immune responses are initiated
The lymphatic system transports immune cells and drains excess tissue fluid
Swollen lymph nodes indicate active immune responses to nearby infections

faq.question: Why do lymph nodes swell when you are sick?
faq.answer: Pathogens draining from infected tissue are captured in nearby lymph nodes, where they activate B and T cells. These cells multiply rapidly within the node, causing it to enlarge. Swollen lymph nodes are a sign your immune system is actively fighting an infection.

faq.question: What happens if the lymphatic system is damaged?
faq.answer: Damage from surgery, radiation, or parasitic infection prevents fluid drainage, causing lymphedema, which is painful swelling. Immune surveillance is also compromised in affected areas because immune cells cannot circulate normally or be delivered to sites of infection.
